scope: Derived classifiers and modular-engine specifications; independent source descriptions remain in 376-position public catalog; not actual implemented game engines.

mechanic_families.name: Trick-Taking
mechanic_families.definition: Each player contributes a card to a trick under rank/suit/trump constraints
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Follow-suit checking, trump resolution, partnership/solo contracts

mechanic_families.name: Combat / Resource
mechanic_families.definition: Cards deploy effects, attacks, defenses and resources
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Costs, damage, zones, event queue, modifier layering

mechanic_families.name: Meld / Set Collection
mechanic_families.definition: Arrange/collect matching ranks, runs or scoring groups

mechanic_families.name: Hand Totals / Banking
mechanic_families.definition: Optimize comparable hands or numerical totals, possibly against dealer
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Hand evaluator, bankroll-free score tracking, rank comparisons

mechanic_families.name: Layout / Spatial
mechanic_families.definition: Cards occupy a tableau/track/network whose position matters
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Legal placement, board topology, lanes/paths, objective checking

mechanic_families.name: Trade / Draft / Deckbuild
mechanic_families.definition: Acquire, pass, exchange or construct playable holdings
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Markets, draft rounds, ownership, deck construction

mechanic_families.name: Cooperative Coordination
mechanic_families.definition: Players share an objective but face communication or information limits
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Team tasks, clue budgets, restricted communication

mechanic_families.name: Deck Tradition / Uncertain Rules
mechanic_families.definition: A physical card system or disputed historical reference rather than a single verified game
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Deck schemas, suit/rank identity, variant registry

mechanic_families.name: Inference / Bluff
mechanic_families.definition: Hidden information is inferred, signaled or strategically misrepresented
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Visibility permissions, bids, clues, reveal rules

mechanic_families.name: Rule / Narrative Mutation
mechanic_families.definition: Cards change rules, attributes, scoring systems or narrative state
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Rule precedence, effect patches, reversible state changes

mechanic_families.name: Shedding / Climbing
mechanic_families.definition: Players dispose of cards while matching rank, suit or value

mechanic_families.name: Risk / Push Your Luck
mechanic_families.definition: Players choose how much uncertainty or failure risk to accept
mechanic_families.rules_primitives: Risk deck, probability state, survival constraints

integrity_constraints: Preserve raw uploaded descriptions independently from interpretation
Do not equate automation with zero required inputs
Do not equate aesthetic void with zero-valued game state
Use checkpoints and an auditable event log for simulation claims
Identify original TABOR concepts as design proposals until implemented

rules: No source positions are deduplicated or rewritten
Historical and commercial claims are user supplied and require independent verification
No engine module is marked as deployed or production ready
Keep third-party intellectual property and original TABOR WORLD IDs separate
ACT authorizations and release review required for any final game
